Redline round 1

Reviewed the whole pull request.

The coverage pass over the whole pull request at 1c96b8c returned 15 candidates: 1 confirmed, 12 for the person, 0 collapsed into findings already reported or settled, 0 already tracked, 2 dropped (refuted, outside the diff or disproportionate).

This PR pins a self-hosted relaunch to the script the run launched with, through `run drift`. It also adds a Finish read that stops a run finishing below the highest posted round. Both come with prefs, loop and guard tests for every answer `run drift` gives and for the refusal. The one finding is in the new agent-change sentence: it reaches the handoff comment through `args.drift`, which the skill recomputes on every relaunch, an error resume included, so a resume after the comment posted can post it again. Most other candidates are gaps in the agent report and in the Finish backstop, listed for the person. This repository has no scheduled or queued work, and the version bump and Docs entries are in place.

### Findings (1 correctness, 0 nit)

- **R1-1** · correctness · medium · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:2990` · A resume after the handoff comment posted posts it again when args.drift changed

Each finding has an inline comment with the detail or, where GitHub could not anchor it, sits under Not placed inline below. Redline replies in the finding's thread, or in a PR comment that opens with its marker, once the round's fixes are committed.

### For the person

- `workflows/redline-loop.js:3134` · The Finish rule stops only when a posted round is above the finishing round. A re-run of the highest posted round itself, whose post is skipped as already posted, still hands off if it comes back clean. It needs the pin to fail first. A check on a skipped post would also stop a legitimate resume at `post rN`, which skips the post and uses the cached findings.
- `skills/redline/SKILL.md:226` · On the plugin's own repository, when `run save` exits 2 the skill follows line 218 ("go on: the relaunch in this session does not need the marker"). The person answers every call, then `run drift` exits 2 and the skill stops, so the answers are lost. Decision 9 chose the stop, but the two sentences now disagree. Saying so at the save, or letting `run drift` read the run's record directly, would avoid it.
- `scripts/redline-prefs.sh:208` · A pin that cannot be found (no record, a record without `scriptPath`, or a persisted copy that is gone) is treated like a launch by the scriptPath fallback. A changed workflow is then refused with a line saying the launch ran from the file itself, which is not the cause in that case. The refusal is safe; only its stated reason is wrong. The harness records read here do carry `scriptPath`.
- `workflows/redline-loop.js:244` · The agent sentence exists only when a relaunch passed `args.drift`. An autopilot self-review that edits an agent file reports nothing, and neither does a guided one that edits one after its last hand-off. The cap-hit comment and a human review summary never carry the sentence. So shape.md's "an agent change is read from git and reported, whatever the session has loaded" holds only at relaunches. That matters if an interactive session does reload agent files mid-session, which was not measured.
- `skills/redline/SKILL.md:224` · Both refusals, the skill's `refuse` and the workflow's stage `relaunch`, run `run clear` without telling the person which uncommitted spec folders the earlier run left. The stage `relaunch` result's `specFolders` is empty, and the marker that named them is cleared. The fresh run's clean-tree precheck then fails without its `commit or remove <folders>` line.
- `workflows/redline-loop.js:245` · The handoff comment is posted after the last round, so "this run's remaining rounds may run under them" reads there as a forecast. Something like "the later rounds may have run under them" would fit. The wording is decision 1's rider, so the change is the author's call.
- `skills/redline/SKILL.md:220` · `run drift` runs only just before the relaunch, after the person has answered the calls. A `refuse` can only follow a launch by the scriptPath fallback, and it could be detected at the stop instead, before any call is presented.
- `workflows/redline-loop.js:3126` · The Finish read also runs in a dry run, where nothing was posted and the check cannot fire. Skipping it when `postToGitHub` is false would save one agent call and one GitHub read. The loop test pins today's dry-run call list.
- `scripts/redline-prefs.sh:227` · The agent sentence and the refusal text are each written twice, in this jq and in the workflow (AGENTS_CHANGED and the stage `relaunch` error). Each copy is pinned by its own test, so an edit to one copy passes while the skill's spoken line and the handoff comment drift apart.
- `scripts/redline-prefs.sh:192` · The self-hosted test (`--plugin` resolves to the repository root) now appears twice in this script, here and in `run check`'s `plugin` reason at line 277. One helper would keep them from disagreeing when #66 changes how self-hosting is detected.
- `workflows/redline-loop.js:3407` · The workflow's second layer fires only when the skill ran `run drift`, got `refuse` and launched anyway with that `drift`. A relaunch that skipped `run drift` arrives with no `args.drift` and is not caught, so the pin depends entirely on the skill following section 7.
- `agent-os/specs/2026-11-12-1852-81-pin-relaunch-script-finish-rule/shape.md:53` · The probe report (harness behaviour measured headless on 2.1.322) is written into this public spec and into two standards. CLAUDE.md keeps spike notes in `redline-internal`, and the #72 spike cited its notes there by file name. This spec says the probes are its own and nothing was copied. Whether a probe report belongs here is the author's call.

### Candidates set aside (2)

<details>
<summary>Collapsed, already tracked or dropped</summary>

- `scripts/redline-gh.sh:315` · Already tracked in #88: `last-round` counts any line, in any review body, that starts with 'Redline round N'. #88 does not say that this PR makes the over-count end a run: Finish now uses that number and stops with a non-resumable error naming a 're-run' that never happened. #88 also covers only Redline's own free text, while a teammate's review body is read the same way. · disproportionate: #88 tracks Redline's own posted text forging a line. The remainder, Finish stopping on an over-count, needs a review body posted during the run, by a teammate or in a moved finding's description, with a line opening `Redline round M` for an M above the round the run is finishing from. Any such line posted before launch is already counted, because the launch's `firstRound` comes from the same `last-round` read.
- `scripts/redline-prefs.sh:215` · `launch: name` is chosen by comparing the pinned copy with the file on disk. A launch by name runs the session's registry, which the spec's probe b measured as loaded at session start or reopen, not the file on disk. When the registry holds a different version than the pin, a 'name' relaunch runs that version and replay diverges. Per the probe, it also overwrites the pin. · disproportionate: Needs two things: a session reopened mid-run after a round changed the workflow file, so the registry holds the edit, and then a later round restoring `workflows/redline-loop.js` byte for byte to the launch's version. Only then does `run drift` answer `name` while the registry would run the edit.

</details>

comments.body:
**R1-1** · correctness · medium · confirmed

**A resume after the handoff comment posted posts it again when args.drift changed**

The handoff comment's text now carries AGENTS_CHANGED, which is built from `args.drift`. Section 7 of the skill (skills/redline/SKILL.md:220-226) has every relaunch rerun `run drift` and set `args.drift` again, and that includes an `error` or `stopped` resume. So the agent list at a resume can differ from the one the Finish launch had. In an autopilot self-review that is true of any agent edit, since autopilot never relaunches before Finish. In a guided one it is true of an agent edit made after the last hand-off. When the lists differ, the `handoff comment` prompt changes even though the comment is already on the PR.

Case 1, a resume at `record files` or `record commit` (for example after a rejected push), or a stopped run relaunched after the comment posted. The harness reruns `handoff comment`, and that prompt has no duplicate check: tests/loop-test.mjs:1207 pins that the handoff comment before a record-commit resume carries no clause. A second Redline handoff comment is posted and review is requested again.

Case 2, a resume at `handoff comment` itself (a review request that failed after the post). The duplicate check looks for a comment with exactly the body of the new file. That body now holds the sentence, so the check finds no match and the comment is posted again.

This breaks the skill's sentence "The workflow reads it only at startup and at Finish, so no replayed prompt depends on it" (SKILL.md:226) and the new workflow/replay.md bullet for Finish's own replayed prompts. Traced through `handoffComment`, `finishPrompt`, `resumeLine` and section 7. The scratch reproduction /tmp/redlinerepro/reviewer-r1-repro.mjs is built on the loop test's mock but could not be run here, because node is refused to this role.

Proposed fix: Keep the Finish prompts stable across attempts. The smallest fix is in the skill: on an `error` or `stopped` resume, pass `args.drift` exactly as the marker's args hold it. Still run `run drift` to choose name, scriptPath or refuse and to say its agent line. Only a hand-off or `reviewed` relaunch sets `args.drift` again. Write this in section 7 and in docs/running.md, "Hand-off and relaunch". The alternative is for the workflow to read the changed agent files itself at Finish, in a GitHub-agent call with a fixed prompt that replays from cache on a resume. That also reports an agent edit in a run that never relaunched. Either way, add a loop-test check: on a `record commit` resume with unchanged args, every prompt through `handoff comment` replays byte for byte, and a different `drift.agents` changes the `handoff comment` prompt. That second half is the risk the rule guards against.
